name: How do you hide or finish the area after pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What are the best ways to finish and hide the former pool footprint after removal?
mainEntity.text: What are the best ways to finish and hide the former pool footprint after removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The former pool footprint can be finished in many ways, but the best option depends on the future use of the yard. Some homeowners want lawn or low-water landscaping, while others want a patio extension, play area, or a prepared pad for future construction. The final design should match the grade and drainage plan so the old pool area blends into the yard and performs well over time. In Southern California, drought-tolerant landscaping is a common choice because it is practical and attractive. Homeowners should coordinate the finish with the demolition contractor or landscape designer so the new surface is built on properly compacted fill and the transitions are smooth. A thoughtful finish makes the removal look intentional instead of like a temporary patch.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best finish depends on the new use of the yard. Common options include lawn, drought-tolerant landscaping, decomposed granite, patio extension, play space, or a future building pad. A good finish should match the site grade, drainage, and long-term plans so the old pool area does not settle or stand out.
